title: Quantum Resources and Performance in the Initialization-Free Bernstein-Vazirani Algorithm
authors: Haesol Han, Alexander Streltsov, Soojoon Lee
abstract: Naseri et al. [Phys. Rev. A 106, 062429 (2022); arXiv:2205.13610] studied which quantum resources in initial states are essential for the probabilistic Bernstein-Vazirani (BV) algorithm, defining its performance as the optimal average success probability over all measurements. In this work, we consider a variant of BV algorithm, which is called the initialization-free (IF) BV algorithm, in which an arbitrary ancilla state as the oracle register is allowed, to improve the performance. We derive an explicit formula for the performance of the probabilistic IF-BV algorithm and obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for an initial state to achieve maximal performance. We further prove that, under a suitable ordering assumption on the coefficients of the initial state, the probabilistic IF-BV algorithm outperforms the standard probabilistic BV algorithm.
summary: This work rigorously analyzes the performance limits of an initialization-free variant of the Bernstein-Vazirani algorithm. By deriving explicit formulas based on initial state coherence, the authors prove that this IF-BV method generally surpasses the standard BV algorithm. The findings provide deep insights into which quantum resources are essential for achieving optimal computational success probabilities.
main_problem: The paper analyzes the performance of an initialization-free variant of the Bernstein-Vazirani (BV) quantum algorithm compared to its standard probabilistic counterpart.
main_result: It derives explicit formulas showing that the IF-BV algorithm generally outperforms the standard BV algorithm, and it establishes necessary and sufficient conditions for achieving maximal success probability.
method: The analysis employs techniques from quantum channel discrimination theory, utilizing Semidefinite Programming (SDP) characterization to derive performance bounds based on initial state coherence properties.
model_or_system: The model is the probabilistic IF-BV algorithm applied to an oracle problem, considering pure initial states $|\muangle = \alpha |+angle|\phi_0angle +  eta |-angle|\phi_1angle$ for the ancilla register.
key_observables: Performance ($P_W$) of the IF-BV algorithm and its comparison to the standard BV performance ($P$).
important_parameters: The coefficients $\alpha,  eta$, and the coherence properties (Robustness of Coherence $R$) of the initial states $|\phi_0angle$ and $|\phi_1angle$.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on pure initial states for deriving closed-form expressions; comparisons often rely on a specific relabeling convention for the standard BV algorithm characterization.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the IF-BV performance, deriving explicit formulas relating it to coherence (Chunk 2), then establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for maximal performance (Theorem 6), and finally proving that IF-BV generally outperforms standard BV under certain assumptions (Theorem 8).
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of quantum advantage in specific quantum algorithms, particularly how modifying initial state preparation can boost computational power, is highly relevant to understanding resource theories in quantum computation.
